decision: Apply the named Norske Skog Saugbrugs industrial-area representative point and preserve the historical Saugbrugsforeningen and Tista sawmill landscape as chronological context.
identityFindings: The named map object represents the active Norske Skog Saugbrugs mill and industrial complex at Tista.
Saugbrugsforeningen was founded in 1859 by sawmill owners associated with the Tista waterfalls and is the historical predecessor of the current company and plant identity.
The current name Norske Skog Saugbrugs dates from the transfer to Norske Skog in 1989.
Tistedalen settlement, the distributed historical sawmills, Tista, waterfalls, power facilities and Halden reactor are related contexts but not the same canonical object.
historicalFindings: Saugbrugsforeningen was established in 1859 as the sawmill owners prepared for the end of sawmill privileges and increased competition.
Operations were progressively developed from sawmilling into planing, mechanical pulp, cellulose, paper and other wood processing.
The industrial site became a major employer and shaped Tistedalen's worker and industrial history.
The current active mill continues the institutional and spatial industrial history, although the modern plant does not equal every historical sawmill site.

representationLimits: The marker represents the active Saugbrugs industrial complex and historical institutional continuity, not every historic sawmill site.
The radius is not a factory, property, process, emergency, safety, emission or operational boundary.
The active plant is access-controlled and the coordinate does not grant entry.
Gameplay must remain on lawful public roads and viewpoints outside gates, fences and technical areas.
Tista, waterfalls, power facilities, Tistedalen settlement and Halden reactor remain separate geographic entities.
